creator: Jerry Thomas (author); engraver of the cut unknown. Publisher Dick & Fitzgerald, New York
date: 1862 (preface dated New York, January 2, 1862). Note: the IA metadata field says 1928, which is a catalogue error; the scan is the Harvard/Radcliffe copy of the original Dick & Fitzgerald edition with the original title page and 'Digitized by Google'.
showsAccordingToSource: Item title: "How to mix drinks: or, The bon-vivant's companion" (Commons: "The bar-tender's guide"). Page printed 77 carries the engraved cut captioned "BLUE BLAZER." and recipe 197's closing paragraph. The source does not name the man in the cut.
storyLink: Anchors 'practice' and 'risk' (F2, F3): the page prints the warning "The novice in mixing this beverage should be careful not to scald himself. To become proficient in throwing the liquid from one mug to the other, it will be necessary to practise for some time with cold water." Also shows the 1862 book (paragraph 0: 'In his 1862 book') and the flaming throw between two mugs.
pdReasonUS: Published in New York in 1862, before 1931.
pdReasonUKEU: Author Jerry Thomas died 1885 (before 1956); the engraver is anonymous and the work is over 150 years old.
captionDraft: The Blue Blazer page in Thomas's 1862 book
creditDraft: Internet Archive / Harvard copy · public domain
altDraft: A printed book page with an engraving of a stout, moustached man in a waistcoat throwing a stream of flame between two mugs, above a paragraph about practising with cold water.
concerns: The cut is not captioned with a name; it is commonly taken to be Thomas himself but the source does not say so, so do not name him in the caption. The image shows the staged throw, which the dossier flags (L3 arcs) as a retelling: it illustrates the book's own cut, not a claim that arcs defied gravity. Page is full book page (2500x3813); the app will probably want to crop to the engraving (about 1000x800 px region near the top) plus caption, which stays sharp at 640 px. Slight scan marks at page top edge. Verified by eye against the OCR text that this is printed p.77 (leaf n81) and p.76 (leaf n80) holds recipe 197's start.
